newsitem.title: UK: Centrica lost three pct of users in southwest U.K..
newsitem.headline: Centrica lost three pct of users in southwest U.K..

text.p: Centrica plc has lost around three percent of its customers in Avon and Dorset to competing gas suppliers in the domestic gas market, chief executive Roy Gardner told a news conference on Thursday.
"The numbers who switched on day one are fairly low, around three percent," he said. "Those who have indicated they will switch are in line with our expectations."

Avon and Dorset were opened to competition for domestic gas supply on February 10. A first pilot area covering Devon, Cornwall and Somerset had opened on April 29 last year, and the initial switching rate there was nearer six percent at the beginning, Gardner said. Around 20 percent of consumers have subsequently switched in the first pilot area.

David Varney, chief executive of BG Plc, which includes the former British Gas pipeline and transport arm TransCo, said there were lessons to be learnt from the pilots before the introduction of nationwide competition next year.

"We're digesting lessons from the first pilot area for systems and for the Network Code (the rule book covering gas movement on TransCo's pipeline system) and we'll see what comes from phase two," he said.
"The systems required to underpin domestic competition are different from those needed for a pilot. We don't know how different yet," he added.
